title: Staggered tenant quota replenishment with usage snapshots
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several tenants on Reserved capacity have reported token usage spikes and transient overage charges around global boundary resets (daily and monthly). Our current reset strategy triggers large concurrent replenishments at UTC boundaries which causes: request throttling, quota reconciliation jitter, and occasional double-counting during multi-region failovers. This ticket implements a staggered replenishment strategy that derives per-tenant replenishment windows from a stable tenant snapshot and applies an idempotent, migration-friendly reset flow.

Goals:
- Eliminate large concurrency spikes at global reset moments by spreading replenishment across a configurable stagger window (default 60 minutes).
- Produce deterministic, auditable snapshots of tenant usage counters before applying resets for correct billing and rollback capability.
- Ensure reserved capacity windows (epoch-based) and rolling windows align with invoice boundaries to avoid drift over time.
- Support backfill/migration path for existing tenants with minimal downtime and strong consistency guarantees for quota accounting.

Design notes & trade-offs:
- Snapshot model: create lightweight tenant usage snapshots (consistent point-in-time token counters) stored in billing ledger with version id. Snapshots are taken per-tenant within the snapshot window to keep I/O bounded. This allows idempotent resets and forensic replay.
- Staggering policy: tenants assigned a deterministic offset derived from tenant_id hash + timezone preference; offsets configurable per plan. This avoids a single hot-schduled job. Drawback: increases time to fully apply global policy (but bounded by configured window).
- Strong vs eventual updates: we use a hybrid approach — snapshot and mark phase use strong consistency, but propagation to cache layers (rate limiter, in-memory quota caches) uses eventual updates with fast TTLs and on-demand reconciliation. This reduces lock contention on the primary quota store.
- Migration: rolling migration job marks tenants as "managed-by-stagger" and creates initial snapshot. We provide a one-click console toggle for enterprise accounts to force immediate migration with caution.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema: add billing.snapshots table (tenant_id, snapshot_ts, token_count, snapshot_version, source_job_id).
2) Controller: snapshot-scheduler service that shards work and writes snapshots; idempotent via snapshot_version.
3) Replenisher: staggered-replenish worker reads snapshots, applies reset delta to tenant quota ledger, emits audit events, invalidates caches.
4) Rate limiter integration: add reconciliation hook to accept snapshot_version and accept reset only if version >= current.
5) Migration job & backfill: a backfill pipeline that safely creates snapshots for pre-existing tenants.
6) Feature flag and rollout: start with non-critical tenants, monitor, then enable for reserved-capacity tenants.

Testing & observability:
- New Grafana dashboards: quota-reset-throughput, snapshot-latency, failed-resets by tenant tier.
- Add SLO: 99.9% successful resets within configured window.
- End-to-end tests: synthetic tenants with cross-region failover scenarios.

Rollout & fallback:
- Stage 1: run snapshot-scheduler in dry-run for 48 hours, publish metrics.
- Stage 2: enable replenish in staging with 10% of tenants (low-risk).
- Stage 3: ramp up to 100% reserved capacity tenants.
- Fallback: replenisher writes compensating adjustments and creates rollback snapshot; console provides "replay reset" action.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: increased DB write amplification. Mitigation: batch snapshot writes and shard by tenant prefix; throttle backfill.
- Risk: stale cache causing temporary over-limit rates. Mitigation: force cache invalidation and short-circuit path for the first hour after reset.
- Risk: billing disputes from edge cases. Mitigation: store full snapshot history and provide a customer-facing reconciliation report for 90 days.

Links & artifacts:
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/ENG-30577+-+Staggered+Quota+Replenishment+RFC
- Design diagram: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/12aBq-staggered-quota-design
- PR (work in progress): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4982
- Grafana dashboard (preview): https://grafana.redwood.com/d/quotareset/quotareset-overview

Success criteria:
- No customer-facing quota throttles caused by global resets for 30 days post-rollout.
- 99.9% of resets complete within configured window.
- Lower peak write throughput on quota service during boundary hours by >=60%.

Next steps (short term):
- Complete snapshot schema migration and small-scale dry-run (Connor).
- Prepare observability queries and Grafana panels (SRE).
- Review PR and run integration tests (Asha/Marina).
